answer: Divergent-drift registration. Each identity must cross a bridge checkpoint that records a signed path history; clones following identical paths collide at the checkpoint and are rejected, while genuine agents diverge naturally like a river splitting around obstacles. A clone farm must give each copy a distinct history, forcing separate crossings and unique timing, which multiplies cost per identity across the tundra of registration overhead. The attacker pays full crossing cost per copy rather than one shared cost.
